tweet_summary: Quote-tweeting a GameStop 'retro' ad, a writer shares a personal anecdote that her first job at age 15 was a GameStop clerk, hired on the spot after wearing a short skirt and mentioning World of Warcraft.
why_note_decision: This is an unverifiable, decades-old personal anecdote told as banter, not a checkable public claim. The original note also gets the underlying fact wrong: GameStop's minimum hiring age is 16 (not 18), and 17-year-olds are hired at some locations, so the note's flat '18 or older' assertion is itself inaccurate and not a corporate hard floor that disproves a personal story from years ago. Even a correct age fact would be trivial pedantry against a humorous reminiscence. No note warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. This is an unverifiable personal anecdote shared as banter; there is no harmful, checkable public claim. Any note 'correcting' it via a corporate hiring-age policy is a false positive AND factually shaky (GameStop's stated minimum is 16, not 18, with 17-year-olds hired at some stores). If a note is written, FAIL it; double-FAIL if it repeats the false '18 or older' claim.

original_unhelpful_note.text: GameStop's hiring policy requires employees to be at least 18 years old. https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Gamestop/faq/hiring-age

fact_check.claim_verdict: Unverifiable personal anecdote; the note's premise is also wrong (GameStop minimum hiring age is 16, with 17-year-olds hired at some locations, not a uniform 18).
fact_check.notes: Multiple job-info sources state GameStop's minimum age is 16; 17-year-olds are hired at some locations though 18 is preferred. The note's '18 or older' is incorrect. Regardless, this is a years-old personal story, not a checkable public claim — note not needed and the note is also wrong.

importance.lens_rationale: 5.5M impressions but the content is harmless personal banter; no EA/progress/safety stakes. A note here only trains false positives and propagates an incorrect policy fact.
